profile.reading: This is one of three data center buildings on Vantage Data Centers' New Albany, Ohio campus at 3325 Horizon Court, in the New Albany International Business Park spanning Licking and Franklin counties, now one of the largest concentrations of hyperscale data center construction in the eastern United States. The park has drawn Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Vantage, attracted by AEP Ohio's transmission capacity, Ohio's data center sales-and-use-tax exemption program, and local economic-development incentive agreements negotiated with New Albany and Licking County. Vantage's own campus materials describe the site as roughly 70 acres with about 1.5 million square feet planned across three two-story buildings, each stated at approximately 64 megawatts of critical IT capacity, for a total campus capacity near 192 megawatts once fully built out; Vantage's page does not assign individual names, building numbers, or separately confirmed square-footage figures to each of the three structures beyond this uniform per-building description, so an even division of the 1.5 million total (approximately 500,000 square feet per building) is this profile's derived estimate rather than an operator-confirmed figure for this specific building. Vantage has stated the first of the three buildings was slated to reach operational status in December 2025, with additional phases continuing through 2028. Power is supplied end-to-end at 480 volts, with N+1 electrical and N+2 mechanical redundancy per Vantage's standard design approach, and each building is targeted for LEED Silver certification. Vantage Data Centers, headquartered in Denver, is backed by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake, which committed $6.4 billion in fresh capital to the company in January 2024. Ohio's rapid data center buildout, concentrated heavily in New Albany and neighboring Licking County communities, has become a subject of statewide debate over electricity rate impacts on residential ratepayers, prompting AEP Ohio to propose a distinct large-load tariff classification for data centers before the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.

reading.body:
Vantage Building 2 is one of three data center structures planned at the New Albany, Ohio campus, each designed for 64 megawatts of critical IT load. The full campus sits on 70 acres in New Albany International Business Park, which has attracted hyperscale construction from Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, and Microsoft alongside Vantage. No capacity figure for this building alone has been published; the operator describes the campus uniformly at 64 MW per building across three structures totaling 192 MW, with phased completion targeted through 2028. The first building was targeted for December 2025 operation, a date now past, but actual delivery has not been independently confirmed.

At the assumed density of 5 megawatts per 100 racks used in modern hyperscale AI training, 64 megawatts of IT load would accommodate roughly 1,280 racks. Power arrives at 480 volts with N+1 electrical and N+2 mechanical redundancy per Vantage's standard design. The building is targeted for LEED Silver certification, which qualifies it for energy-efficiency recognition but does not confirm grid impact or PUE. Neither electrical interconnection details nor primary power supply agreements have been published.

Ohio has mapped five data center facilities total but published power capacity from none. This Vantage campus is the only facility in the state with a published megawatt figure on record here, giving it rank one by that single metric. The New Albany International Business Park concentration has prompted the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio to examine whether data center load requires a separate large-load tariff classification to protect residential electricity rates, signaling that the state views this cluster as material to grid planning.
